reason: The text demonstrates Moses actively taking accountability for the Hebrew people's welfare. Throughout this passage, Moses is portrayed as their advocate and leader who directly intercedes with Pharaoh on their behalf (וַיֹּאמֶר מֹשֶׁה לְפַרְעֹה...), carries out divine instructions to free them from bondage, and orchestrates the plagues to secure their liberation. Moses and Aaron together execute the miraculous signs (וּמֹשֶׁה וְאַהֲרֹן עָשׂוּ אֶת־ כָּל־ הַמֹּפְתִים), and Moses continuously appears before Pharaoh to demand the release of his people. This demonstrates sustained leadership responsibility and accountability for the people's condition, not indifference or shirking of duty. The narrative clearly portrays Moses as an engaged leader who takes concrete action to address the plight of his people.
